anthropic_claude_news.title: Anthropic May Go Public This Month, Aims To Top SpaceX's Record IPO Size
anthropic_claude_news.summary: Anthropic is reportedly in discussions to go public as soon as this month, with bankers targeting a raise that would top SpaceX's record IPO. Terms are still moving and nothing is confirmed, but a listing of that size would make Claude's roadmap a public-markets story rather than a private one. Automation angle: An IPO-bound Anthropic means enterprise Claude adoption gets a marketing budget — position your Claude Code portfolio pieces now, while 'built on Claude' is still a differentiator on a junior CV.

anthropic_claude_news.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
anthropic_claude_news.summary: TechCrunch ran a series of jailbreak tests against Claude Opus 4.6 and found the model's ban on sexually explicit output was easy to talk past. Anthropic's usage policy forbids the content, so the gap is enforcement, not policy. Automation angle: If you ship a Claude-powered agent for a client, the safety layer is YOUR job too — an output-side filter plus a logged refusal test suite is a small, very demo-able portfolio project.

ai_business_automation.title: Dutch regulator fines Uber $966 million for automating driver suspensions
ai_business_automation.summary: The Dutch data-protection regulator fined Uber $966 million for using an automated algorithmic system to suspend drivers without adequate human review — the second-largest GDPR penalty ever issued. The violation was the AI-driven decision itself, not the data handling around it, which puts every automated decisioning workflow on notice. Automation angle: Any workflow that automates a decision about a person needs a documented human-review step. Build the review queue into the automation and you can sell it in the EU at all.

ai_business_automation.title: Netflix tests language model as alternative to hand-built recommendation logic
ai_business_automation.summary: Netflix put a language model head-to-head against the hand-built recommendation engine it has tuned for years, testing whether a general model can replace bespoke ranking logic. It is the clearest example yet of LLMs eating classical ML pipelines inside a big product. Automation angle: The pattern to copy: replace one crufty rules engine with an LLM, keep the old one running as the control, and report the delta. That comparison IS the portfolio piece.

ai_business_automation.title: Patients Are Skipping Going to the Doctor Because AI “Receptionists” Can’t Understanding What They’re Saying
ai_business_automation.summary: Patients are abandoning appointment bookings because AI phone receptionists cannot parse what they are saying, with callers simply hanging up rather than retrying. Healthcare front-desk automation is being deployed faster than it is being evaluated. Automation angle: Voice agents fail on accents, interruptions and edge intents — a fallback-to-human path plus a transcript eval harness is the deliverable clinics will actually pay for.

quantum_ai_research.title: Quantum X Labs Tests AI Quantum Error Decoder on Google Hardware Dataset
quantum_ai_research.summary: Quantum X Labs benchmarked its machine-learning quantum error decoder against Google's published hardware dataset, testing whether a learned decoder beats the standard algorithmic ones on real device noise. Error correction is where AI is currently most useful to quantum hardware, because the noise is empirical rather than analytic. Automation angle: Learned decoders are ML on messy real-world telemetry — the same shape as the anomaly detection work that entry-level AI automation roles actually hire for.

quantum_ai_research.title: Reinforcement LearningtoHarness Approximation Errors for Long-Time QuantumSimulation
quantum_ai_research.summary: RL-Trotter, from an arXiv quant-ph paper, uses reinforcement learning to treat the unavoidable approximation errors in digital quantum simulation as a correction resource rather than pure loss. It is AI reshaping the algorithm, not just tuning its parameters. Automation angle: The reframe is portable: instead of suppressing your pipeline's error signal, feed it back as an input the agent can act on.

quantum_ai_research.title: QUASAR: A Quantum-Classical Neural Network for SAR Satellite Physical-Layer Authentication
quantum_ai_research.summary: QUASAR proposes a hybrid quantum-classical neural network for physical-layer authentication of X-band SAR satellites, a security layer that sits orthogonal to cryptography. It is one of the few quantum-ML papers with a concrete deployed-system target. Automation angle: Hybrid quantum-classical architectures still run their classical half on ordinary ML infrastructure — the deployment skills transfer directly.

quantum_ai_research.title: ChatGPT Solves All Tested Qiskit Homework Assignments
quantum_ai_research.summary: A study found ChatGPT completed every tested Qiskit homework assignment, breaking the assessment model for quantum software courses. The authors examine whether such coursework can stay autogradable while still requiring students to run and defend their code. Automation angle: Same assessment collapse hits every coding bootcamp certificate — which is precisely why a public repo of working automations outranks a course badge.

quantum_ai_research.title: WiMi's Next-Generation Quantum Convolutional Neural Network Reshapes Classical Data Classification Methods - TradingView
quantum_ai_research.summary: WiMi published work on a next-generation quantum convolutional neural network aimed at classical data classification, claiming better feature extraction than conventional CNN layers. Vendor-published results, so read the benchmark before the headline. Automation angle: Quantum-CNN claims are still corporate-comms grade — a useful reminder to check who ran the benchmark before you repeat a model claim in an interview.

quantum_ai_research.title: Teaching AI with Quantum Data - Quantinuum
quantum_ai_research.summary: Quantinuum makes the reverse argument: rather than using AI to run quantum machines, use quantum-generated data to train AI models, on the grounds that quantum systems produce distributions classical simulators cannot cheaply fake. Automation angle: 'Where does training data nobody else has come from' is the most valuable question in applied AI — worth asking of every client dataset you touch.

quantum_ai_research.title: FormationQ and STFC Hartree Centre Partner to Drive Enterprise Quantum and AI Adoption in the UK - Quantum Computing Report
quantum_ai_research.summary: FormationQ and the STFC Hartree Centre launched a UK partnership to push enterprise adoption of quantum and AI together, aimed at firms with no in-house expertise in either. It is an adoption-programme play rather than a research result. Automation angle: Publicly funded adoption programmes are a real route into paid AI work without prior experience — check whether they take external implementation partners.

quantum_ai_research.title: When the Quantum-AI Invention Stack Speeds Up Discovery, Patent Practice Has to Move Upstream - IPWatchdog.com
quantum_ai_research.summary: IPWatchdog argues that as the combined quantum-AI stack accelerates discovery, patent practice has to move upstream to capture inventions made partly by machine. Who counts as the inventor when an AI system proposed the design is still unresolved. Automation angle: Attribution of AI-assisted work is becoming a contract clause — settle IP ownership in writing before you deliver an agent-built system to a client.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Grok 4.6 and Grok Bot Expand xAI’s Push Into AI Agents - Techgenyz
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: xAI is pushing Grok 4.6 and the new Grok Bot squarely into agent territory, positioning the pair as a build-and-run stack rather than a chat model. The framing matches xAI's recent releases: model quality plus a harness that executes. Automation angle: The 'model + harness' packaging is exactly what n8n/Claude Code workflows already do — build one agent twice (Grok and Claude) and you own the comparison every interviewer asks about.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Grok 4.6 on Google Enterprise Agent Platform - x.ai
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Grok 4.6 is now available on Google's enterprise agent platform, adding a third major cloud distribution channel alongside its existing enterprise listings. xAI is clearly chasing enterprise procurement, not just consumer subscriptions. Automation angle: Multi-cloud model availability means clients will ask for model-agnostic pipelines — keep your automations behind a router abstraction instead of hardcoding one vendor.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Grok Voice ranked first - x.com
elon_musk_ai_vision.source: Elon Musk on X (via Google News)
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Elon Musk flagged that Grok Voice took the top spot in a voice-assistant ranking, part of a steady drumbeat of xAI leaderboard claims this week. Treat the ranking as vendor-sourced until an independent eval confirms it. Automation angle: Voice agents are the fastest-growing freelance automation niche — a working voice intake bot is a stronger portfolio piece than another text chatbot.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: It’s that easy to use Grok @bot - x.com
elon_musk_ai_vision.source: Elon Musk on X (via Google News)
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Musk spent the day demoing how little setup Grok @bot needs, pitching it as an agent an ordinary user can point at a task and walk away from. The pitch is ease-of-use, aimed at the same audience no-code automation tools serve. Automation angle: Watch the onboarding flow, not the model: whoever makes agent setup a 60-second job wins this market, and that UX lesson transfers straight into how you package client automations.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: This Is Probably Not the AI-Generated Version of “The Odyssey” That Elon Musk Was Imagining
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Futurism took apart the AI-generated 'Odyssey' adaptation circulating this week, a project Musk had publicly cheered on, and found the output well short of the promise. It is a useful check on the 'AI replaces creative production' line Musk keeps advancing. Automation angle: Public AI-slop backlash is a positioning gift: sell 'AI that does the boring middle of the workflow', not 'AI that replaces the creative work'.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Psychological methods reveal major weaknesses in AI security testing
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Researchers applied psychological measurement methods to AI security evaluations and found the tests are far weaker than their scores suggest — they measure inconsistently and do not generalise. Everyone reports safety-eval numbers; almost nobody validates the eval itself. Affected: every team relying on a vendor's published safety scores for procurement. Automation angle: Nobody sells 'evals for your evals' yet. A reproducible test harness that re-runs a vendor's own safety claims against your prompts is an unusually differentiated offer.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: World models that ignore human beliefs predict the wrong actions, new research shows
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Current world models such as Sora or Genie simulate physical dynamics but ignore what the people in the scene believe, so they predict the wrong actions whenever behaviour depends on belief rather than physics. It is a structural gap in video-world-model research, and no shipped system addresses it. Affected: anyone building agents that must anticipate human behaviour rather than object motion. Automation angle: Agent planning has the same hole — your automations need an explicit model of what the user thinks is happening, not just what the system state is.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: The Results of Middle and High School Students Using AI Are Extremely Ominous
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: New results on middle- and high-school students using AI show grades holding up while actual learning does not, meaning the standard assessment no longer measures the thing it claims to. Schools have deployment policies but no working way to detect the gap. Affected: every institution using graded output as a proxy for capability. Automation angle: The same measurement failure hits AI-assisted hiring tests — process evidence (commits, logs, iterations) is now worth more than a finished artefact, so publish yours.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: AI-Generated Children’s Stories Contain Bizarre Patterns
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: An analysis of AI-generated children's stories found the same tropes recurring across outputs — visible mode collapse in a product category being shipped to kids right now. Diversity of generated output has no standard metric and no vendor accountability. Affected: publishers and parents buying AI-generated material at scale. Automation angle: Output-diversity scoring across a batch of generations is a genuinely missing tool, and a neat small project to build and publish.

ai_business_opportunities.title: Only 9% of India's finance aspirants feel ready to compete in AI-driven job market: Study
ai_business_opportunities.summary: Only 9% of India's finance graduates feel ready for an AI-driven job market and 56% say AI is making job hunting harder — a training gap with a large, self-identified audience. Build: a 4-week 'AI ops for finance teams' cohort teaching one reconciliation, one reporting and one intake automation on n8n plus an LLM. Buyer: finance graduates and the mid-size firms that hire them. Why now: the readiness gap is measured and public, so the pain is pre-qualified. Automation angle: Teach the exact three workflows you can already build — the course doubles as the portfolio, and the cohort becomes your first set of testimonials.

ai_business_opportunities.title: Devious New Font Turns AI Scrapers Into Mincemeat
ai_business_opportunities.summary: A new font that deliberately corrupts text for AI scrapers is getting attention precisely because publishers have no enforceable opt-out — poisoning is what people build when consent has no plumbing. Build: a scrape-consent and provenance service — a 'who took my content' report, machine-readable licence terms and an evidence log for takedowns. Buyer: mid-size publishers, course creators and agencies with content libraries. Why now: AI licensing deals are being signed weekly and nobody below enterprise scale can prove what was taken. Automation angle: Start with the reporting half — a weekly 'AI crawlers that hit your site' digest is buildable in a weekend and gets you the sales conversation.

ai_business_opportunities.title: 'I can't stop': 80% of developers find AI coding more addictive than helpful
ai_business_opportunities.summary: 80% of developers report AI coding tools feel addictive rather than helpful, and no vendor measures it. Build: a lightweight usage-telemetry and guardrail service for engineering teams — rework rate, time-to-verify, prompts per merged PR, plus budget caps per repo. Buyer: engineering managers at 20-200 person companies who have rolled out Copilot or Claude Code and cannot tell if it worked. Why now: adoption is universal and measurement is absent. Automation angle: Start by instrumenting your own repos and publishing the dashboard — the artefact is the sales pitch.

global_ai_news.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
global_ai_news.summary: OpenAI is now asking California to strengthen SB 53, the state AI safety bill it opposed earlier in the process. The reversal matters because SB 53's disclosure duties would apply to every frontier lab operating in the state. Automation angle: Compliance reporting is about to become an automation line item — a workflow that collects model-eval evidence into an audit trail is a real, sellable build.

global_ai_news.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
global_ai_news.summary: A new study of frontier labs found almost no publicly documented plans for containing a model that starts behaving unexpectedly. Labs publish capability evals; containment procedure is where the disclosure stops. Automation angle: Ship a kill-switch with every agent you deploy — scoped credentials, a spend cap and a hard stop are two hours of work and the first thing a serious client checks.

global_ai_news.title: The Unlikely Place at the Center of China’s AI Boom
global_ai_news.summary: Wired traced a chunk of China's AI capacity to a city in Inner Mongolia, where cheap power, spare land and proximity to Beijing turned it into a data-centre hub. Compute geography is becoming an energy-policy question everywhere. Automation angle: Power and location now set inference latency and price — worth knowing which region your client's model endpoint actually runs in before you promise a response-time SLA.

global_ai_news.title: Nvidia invests in data center developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure
global_ai_news.summary: Nvidia has taken an investment stake in data-centre developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure, funding site development while supporting the AI compute buildout on top. Nvidia keeps financing the demand it also supplies. Automation angle: Follow the buildout money to find where AI hiring lands 12 months later — infra regions are where entry-level AI ops roles quietly open up.

global_ai_news.title: Orbital data center startup Starcloud valued at $2.3 billion in latest funding
global_ai_news.summary: Starcloud, which is building orbital data centres for AI compute, was valued at $2.3 billion in its latest round, riding renewed investor appetite for space infrastructure after SpaceX's IPO. Putting AI training capacity in orbit is now a funded thesis, not a thought experiment. Automation angle: Frontier-infra rounds like this are the top of the funnel for the tooling layer — the boring monitoring and orchestration software around them is where a solo builder can actually compete.

global_ai_news.title: Apple cuts jobs in Siri, Vision Pro immersive video and gaming teams
global_ai_news.summary: Apple is cutting staff across the Siri, Vision Pro immersive-video and gaming teams, largely shutting the Vision Pro gaming group while it re-points spending at its AI assistant work. The reshuffle reads as consolidation behind AI, not retreat from it. Automation angle: Big-tech AI reorgs push experienced people into the contractor market — a good moment to look for remote AI-ops work at the mid-size companies picking them up.

indian_ai_industry.title: AI volumes may outweigh revenue deflation for IT sector by FY30: Report
indian_ai_industry.summary: CLSA expects AI-driven volume growth to outrun the pricing deflation it is currently causing in Indian IT services, but not until around FY30. In the meantime productivity gains get passed to clients as lower rates. Automation angle: Indian IT is pricing AI work by outcome, not headcount — build one automation that provably removes a recurring task and you have the exact case study those firms buy.

indian_ai_industry.title: VCs becoming marginal in AI cycle, enterprises should invest in the sector: Peak XV’s Shailendra Singh
indian_ai_industry.summary: Peak XV's Shailendra Singh argued at the ET World Leaders Forum that VCs are becoming marginal in this AI cycle and that large enterprises should be the ones deploying capital, citing HCLTech's stake in Sarvam AI and Amazon's backing of Anthropic. Corporate balance sheets, not funds, are where the AI money now sits. Automation angle: If enterprises are the buyers AND the investors, sell into their internal automation budgets — a working pilot beats a pitch deck with this audience.

indian_ai_industry.title: AI capex slowdown could derail India's cyclical recovery, weigh on growth: Nuvama
indian_ai_industry.summary: Nuvama warned that a slowdown in the global AI capex boom would hit India's cyclical recovery, dragging on corporate revenue and credit growth through weaker global demand. India's upturn is more exposed to AI spending than it looks. Automation angle: Macro risk to watch: if AI capex cools, budget shifts from big platform projects to cheap point automations — which is the exact work a solo builder wins.

indian_ai_industry.title: Engineering graduates should turn India into AI creator rather than mere consumer market, says Delhi CM
indian_ai_industry.summary: Delhi's Chief Minister told engineering graduates that India should become an AI creator rather than a consumer market for other countries' models. The line lands alongside the readiness-gap data from the same day. Automation angle: Government AI rhetoric usually precedes government AI budgets — track IndiaAI programme calls for the hackathon and grant slots they open up.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: AI4AI-Bench asks a sharp version of the recursive self-improvement question: can an LLM agent improve the training algorithm that produces the next AI system, so the improvement compounds? The benchmark scores agents on algorithmic design rather than task performance. Automation angle: Benchmarking agents on the process that builds systems, not the systems, is the same instinct as measuring your workflow instead of your one-off output.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: Phantom Gains audits self-improvement claims in language models against a measured null, and finds that per-problem gain/loss tracking across noisy evaluations produces apparent improvement that is really measurement artefact. Several reported self-improvement results do not survive the control. Automation angle: Always run the null. Before you claim your agent improved a client's process, measure the same period with the agent off.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: AI’s recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all - MIT Technology Review
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: MIT Technology Review pushes back on the industry's boldest current claim — that AI will shortly start improving itself — arguing the compounding loop is much further off than the pitch decks suggest. It is the most cited counterweight to the fast-takeoff narrative this week. Automation angle: Useful interview calibration: talk about compounding automation of YOUR workflow, not speculative AGI timelines.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: The Download: AI’s self-improvement problem, and what’s driving the heat
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: MIT Tech Review's Download expands the same thread, laying out where recursive self-improvement actually stalls: evaluation noise, data limits and the cost of each additional loop. The bottleneck it identifies is measurement, not model capability. Automation angle: If measurement is the bottleneck for labs, it is the bottleneck for your automations too — build the eval before the agent.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Unitree bets on 'self-evolving' AI to accelerate robot revolution - China Daily
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: Unitree is betting on 'self-evolving' AI to speed up its robot programme, framing continuous on-robot learning as the route past hand-tuned control. Claims are company-sourced and the mechanism is not published, so treat the label carefully. Automation angle: Self-evolving is the current marketing word for online learning — ask exactly what gets updated and how often before you believe (or repeat) it.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: SkillForge has LLM agents self-distil project-specific knowledge from a repository so they stop failing on codebase-specific conventions. It is a concrete, working instance of an agent improving itself for a target environment. Automation angle: This is CLAUDE.md formalised — every repo you work in should accumulate a written memory of its own conventions, and that habit is directly demonstrable.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: Task-CoEvolve optimises an LLM agent's harness by iteratively rewriting the harness code against adaptively selected validation tasks, achieving real gains without touching model weights. The scaffold, not the model, is the thing being improved. Automation angle: Your harness — prompts, tools, retries, checks — is the part you actually control. Version it and measure changes to it like code.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Auditing and Decomposing Feedback-Driven Evolution in LLM Test Generation under the Oracle Problem
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: This audit decomposes feedback-driven evolution in LLM test generation and shows that using a single accepted program as ground truth manufactures spurious fault detections, so the loop reports improvement that is not there. The oracle problem quietly breaks the self-improvement signal. Automation angle: If your agent grades its own work against its own output, it will report success forever — always put an independent check in the loop.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Text / LLM - Best: Claude Mythos 5 / Runner-up: GPT-5.6 Sol
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Current category leader: Claude Mythos 5; runner-up GPT-5.6 Sol. Mythos 5 is Anthropic's top-end model this cycle; GPT-5.6 Sol just got a >20% price cut. Automation angle: switch your portfolio demos to whichever model ranks best in the category you build in this week.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Coding - Best: Grok 4.6 (extra-high thinking) / Runner-up: Claude Opus 4.8
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Current category leader: Grok 4.6 (extra-high thinking); runner-up Claude Opus 4.8. Grok 4.6 took #1 on CursorBench this week in extra-high-thinking mode. Automation angle: switch your portfolio demos to whichever model ranks best in the category you build in this week.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Image Generation - Best: ChatGPT Images 2.0 / Runner-up: Midjourney v7

Automation angle: Switch your portfolio demos to whichever model ranks best on coding/agent benchmarks this week — and say why you switched.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Qwen 3.8 27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Qwen 3.8 27B scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — level with GPT-5.6 Luna (max) and a single point behind GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4 Pro. A 27B open-weights model landing in that band changes what you can run locally. Automation angle: An open 27B at frontier-adjacent quality means client work with data-residency rules is now buildable on self-hosted models — a strong, in-demand niche.

new_ai_tools.title: More than just code review
new_ai_tools.summary: Simon Willison argues the core skill with coding agents is not reading every generated line but confidently instructing them and then confidently verifying the result. He walks through what verification actually looks like beyond line-by-line review. Automation angle: This is the Claude Code workflow to demo in an interview: a written instruction, an automated check that proves the change landed, and the diff. Practise the verify half.

new_ai_tools.title: Study explains why AI agents benefit from "skills" and when they fail
new_ai_tools.summary: Princeton and UC San Diego researchers found that agent 'skills' help mainly by imposing structured workflows, not by adding knowledge — and that gains degrade as the skill library grows. It puts a measurable ceiling on the skills pattern Claude Code and similar harnesses use. Automation angle: Keep your skill/tool library small and workflow-shaped. Fewer, sharper skills beat a sprawling library, and that finding is a strong 'why I build it this way' answer.

new_ai_tools.title: OpenAI cuts developer pricing for frontier GPT-5.6 Sol model by more than 20%
new_ai_tools.summary: OpenAI's frontier API price cut of more than 20% reaches Codex and ChatGPT Work credits, changing the cost floor for agentic coding tools. Codex just got materially cheaper to run at volume. Automation angle: Re-run your cost-per-task numbers across Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build this week — a current pricing comparison is a genuinely useful piece of content to publish.

new_ai_tools.title: RayNeo's new AI glasses skip the camera, focus on text overlays
new_ai_tools.summary: RayNeo's new AI glasses drop the camera and speakers entirely, betting on text overlays as the core interaction. Stripping the sensors sidesteps most of the privacy backlash that has dogged camera-equipped smart glasses. Automation angle: Constraint-driven product design is the lesson — cutting a capability to kill an objection works for agents too (no write access, no autonomous spend).

general_news.title: Carney calls Trump's fresh tariffs a 'miscalculation' after trade talks collapse
general_news.summary: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney called Washington's fresh tariffs a 'miscalculation' after trade talks collapsed, and announced retaliatory measures he said he was imposing reluctantly. He accused the US of starting a trade war.

general_news.title: Rescuers dig through Ukraine mall wreckage as Zelensky condemns 'despicable' Russian strike
general_news.summary: Rescuers are still digging through the wreckage of a Ukrainian shopping mall struck on Friday, with four people missing after an attack that killed 16 and injured 130, including children. President Zelensky called the strike despicable.

general_news.title: Fourteen killed in strike on Myanmar monastery
general_news.summary: Fourteen people were killed in a strike on a monastery in Myanmar where civilians had gathered for a meditation retreat. A rescue worker said the site was hit twice.

general_news.title: 2 Cops Among 7 Killed After Vehicle Rams Police Car In England
general_news.summary: Seven people including two police officers were killed in England after a vehicle rammed a police car. Police say they are still investigating the circumstances of the collision.

general_news.title: How 'Dark' Tankers In Strait Of Hormuz Are Keeping Oil Prices In Check
general_news.summary: So-called 'dark' tankers moving through the Strait of Hormuz are helping hold oil prices down despite regional tension, while Middle Eastern producers increasingly route crude away from the strait entirely.

general_news.title: Top US Army Official To Step Down After Months Of Tension With Hegseth: Report
general_news.summary: The top US Army official is stepping down after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, according to reports; the army secretary and his family have already moved out of the official residence.

general_news.title: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record
general_news.summary: A humanoid robot ran 100m in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, beating Usain Bolt's world record time on the track.

general_news.title: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
general_news.summary: Harry and Meghan return to the UK without working-royal status, and are still searching for a public role and a brand identity that lands.
